transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. 

I'm an electrician, and it's probably nothing major—just normal stress, you know?—but I just can't seem to keep my focus on one estimate or, like, a code form anymore. It’s a little embarrassing to admit, but if I hear a tool noise on the site, or my phone gets a text, or even if I just get some new idea about rearranging the workshop, I get pulled completely off track. And then... well, some of the jobs have started getting a little mixed up. 

I really want to do good work and not let my clients down, so I figured I should come see you before it becomes a real issue. Does that sound like a good reason to be here?
Have you always had trouble staying focused like this, even back in school as a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

Oh, no, not back in school. I was actually pretty good at getting my work done as a kid, I promise. This is definitely more recent. 

I guess... well, it’s been building for about seven months now? That’s right around the time we took on the mortgage for the workshop and, you know, all the new equipment. So it's probably just the pressure from that, right? I mean, I figure anybody would get a little scattered with a big loan hanging over them. I'm really trying to handle it responsibly and push through it, though. Does that make sense, that it would start up around then?

Aside from the workshop loan and job performance, have you noticed yourself worrying excessively or feeling on edge about other areas of your life—like your health, family, or finances in general—over these past several months?

No, not really. I mean, I worry a little bit, just like anyone else, I guess. But I wouldn't say I'm on edge about my health or my family or anything like that. My wife and kids are doing great, and I'm healthy. It's really just the work stuff and the loan that's been on my mind. 

I try not to let things get to me too much, you know? I want to be the strong one for my family. So, I just focus on working hard and providing. I hope that's normal... is it normal to just have that one main thing you're stressed about?

Besides losing focus, have you noticed any new problems with your memory—like forgetting recent conversations, misplacing things, or having trouble learning new information—over these past several months?

No, my memory is actually pretty solid, I think. I mean, I might misplace a tool every now and then, but that's just because the site gets messy, you know? It's nothing serious. I definitely haven't forgotten any conversations or anything like that. I always try to be really present when people are talking to me, especially my clients and my wife. 

I'm pretty good at picking up new things, too. Like, I just learned how to use this new diagnostic meter for work, and I got the hang of it right away. So, yeah, I'd say my memory is working just fine. I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means the focus thing really is just stress and not something worse?
Since this stress began about seven months ago, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling down, less interested in things you used to enjoy, or changes in your sleep or appetite?

No, I wouldn't say I've felt down or anything. I mean, I still enjoy my work, and I love spending time with my family on the weekends. We still do our Sunday barbecues, and I look forward to that just as much as I always have. 

My appetite is fine, too. My wife's a great cook, so I definitely make sure to eat well. And sleep... well, I sleep okay. Sometimes it takes me a little bit to wind down after a long day at the site, but I get my rest. I try to make sure I'm taking care of myself so I can keep providing, you know? I really want to make sure I'm doing all the right things. That all sounds pretty healthy, doesn't it?
When you think about the workshop loan and the new equipment costs, do you notice yourself feeling anxious or preoccupied with worry about it, even when you're not actively working?

Well, I mean... I do think about it sometimes when I'm home. But I wouldn't say I'm, like, preoccupied or overly anxious about it. It's just normal business stuff, right? Like, anyone taking out a loan to expand their business is going to run the numbers in their head every now and then. 

I try really hard to leave work at work, though. When I'm with my wife and kids, I want to be fully there for them. So if the loan pops into my head while we're watching TV or something, I just kind of push it aside. I think I manage it pretty well, honestly. It's good to care about your business and want it to succeed, right? That just shows I'm responsible, don't you think?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a 7-month history of concentration difficulties and distractibility that began coincident with an identifiable psychosocial stressor (taking on a business loan and new equipment costs), leading to work errors (functional impairment). Symptoms are restricted to this specific stressor domain rather than pervasive, uncontrollable worry across multiple life areas (ruling out GAD), and there is no evidence of depressed mood, anhedonia, sleep/appetite disturbance (ruling out depressive disorder), no childhood-onset attention symptoms (ruling out ADHD), and no memory or learning deficits (ruling out a cognitive disorder). The clinical picture—emotional/behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, causing impairment in occupational functioning, without meeting criteria for another specific disorder—is most consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety/Mixed features (F43.2).
